messages:
Sam: :rotating_light: ap-southeast-1 P95 jumped to 2.8s in the last 5m, errors creeping on some realtime routes. Anyone looking?
infra-bot: Alert: region=ap-southeast-1 metric=latency_p95 value=2.82s window=5m
Maya (oncall): On it. Can someone dump KV cache metrics + batching stats for the affected pools?
Marta: Pulling metrics now — kv_cache_evictions spiked ~x10 since 13:12 UTC, batch_sizes for chat-route rose to 48 (expected 8-12).
Devon: That smells like the continuous-batching change we rolled Monday. Could be over-aggregating when hotpool backpressure hits.
Lee: Also seeing hotpool utilization at 96% on a subset of GPUs, provisioning is queuing because GCP regional quota is low for ap-southeast-1 this week.
Sam: Ugh. So two drivers: runtime change increasing batch size + insufficient hot capacity leading to longer scheduling waits + cache churn. Need quick mitigations.
Maya (oncall): Prioritize mitigations with least blast radius: 1) throttle batching size for chat-route 2) turn off continuous-batching globally if quick 3) route a % of traffic to eu-west for heavy customers
Devon: I can flip batching throttle. Patch config API: 
```
POST /admin/feature/continuous_batching
{ "enabled": false }
```
I’ll do a targeted throttle first: set max_batch=12 for routes matching `/v1/chat`
Marta: Applying throttle now to prod-apac routing group.
infra-bot: Deploy started: config-change user=Devon action=set_max_batch target=apac-routes
Marta: Throttle applied — batch_size_p95 dropped to ~10 within 30s.
Lee: Starting traffic shift config to route 20% of top customers in apac to eu-west fallback pool. Note: cross-region egress will add $xk/hr.
Sam: Do it. Prefer cost > outage. Add emergency tag to billing.
Maya (oncall): Routing rule applied, 20% shifted. Monitoring p95 and errors.
infra-bot: TrafficShift: region=ap-southeast-1 -> eu-west percent=20 status=ok
Marta: KV evictions reduced ~60% after batching throttle + partial shift. P95 trending down to 1.1s.
Devon: Good. I still want to revert the continuous-batching heuristic in runtime repo — opening revert PR. https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2345
Sam: Can we also enable thin-fallback mode for any requests that hit hotpool queue > 500ms? That will reduce tail latency but may reduce quality for some models.
Lee: Enabled thin-fallback rule via routing policy. Command: 
```
POST /admin/routing/policy
{ "rule": "hotpool_queue_ms>500 -> use_thin_fallback=true" }
```
infra-bot: Policy applied user=Lee rule=hotpool_fallback
Maya (oncall): With all mitigations (throttle, route shift, thin-fallback) apac p95 is back to 0.95s and errors are within SLA.
Sam: Awesome. Next steps: 1) request additional GPU quota/capacity for apac 2) revert or fix batching heuristic in runtime 3) run canary for new batching with tighter limits 4) cost review for cross-region routing
Marta: Filed INC-4217 with capacity and quota owners, attaching timeline and metrics.
Devon: Revert PR linked, will follow up with a safer batching rollout plan.
Lee: Logged a cost tag on the traffic-shift, we should rotate customers back as capacity stabilizes.
Maya (oncall): Incident mark: mitigated -> monitoring. Will keep watch for 2 hours. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Sam: Thanks — postmortem once we verify root cause and cost impact.
Marta: Saving logs and snapshots to the incident channel.
infra-bot: Incident update: mitigated_by=[batch_throttle, traffic_shift, thin_fallback] status=monitoring
